segments.text: Welcome to the IFC coordinator demonstration. This walkthrough covers the key features available to company coordinator users. We'll start at the login page where the coordinator will sign in, then explore every major module in detail.
segments.caption: IFC Coordinator Demo

segments.text: Here at the login page, the coordinator enters their credentials — coordinator dot alembic at gmail dot com — and signs in. Once authenticated, we land on the company admin home dashboard, which serves as the central command center for all IFC activities.
segments.caption: Coordinator Login

segments.text: The dashboard provides an at-a-glance view of critical metrics: pending change requests, ineffective RACMs flagged for review, upcoming deadlines, and recent activity across all modules. Notice the notification badges — one RACM pending change request and one RACM found ineffective — these will be important later in the change request and deficiency response sections.
segments.caption: Dashboard Overview

segments.text: First, User Management. Navigating to the User Management module, administrators can view, add, edit, and manage all users in the organization. The grid displays each user's name, email, assigned roles, business units, and current status. You can filter by role, unit, or status. To add a new user, click the Add User button — this opens a form where you enter details, assign roles such as process owner, approver, or coordinator, and set their business unit permissions. The role-based access control ensures each user only sees what they need. We'll fill in the form fields but stop before submitting to avoid creating a test user.
segments.caption: User Management

segments.text: Next is RACM Communication. This module handles all communications related to Risk and Control Matrices. You can view a complete history of notifications sent, including change request alerts, deficiency notifications, approval reminders, and escalation emails. Each communication shows the recipient, subject, timestamp, and delivery status. The toolbar lets you compose new messages, attach documents, and select distribution lists. There's also a template library for common notification types. We'll open a sample communication to show the detail view with full threading and audit trail.
segments.caption: RACM Communication

segments.text: RACM Templates provides a library of pre-built templates for common control frameworks like SOX, COSO, and custom organizational standards. The template grid shows each template's name, version, framework, last modified date, and status. You can preview any template by clicking its name — this opens a read-only view showing all sections, control objectives, risk categories, and predefined columns. The Import function allows you to bring in templates from Excel or CSV files. We'll click Import to show the file selection and mapping preview. You can also customize templates by adding columns — we'll demonstrate adding a dummy column named 'Test Column' to an existing template, walking through the column type selection, but we'll cancel before saving to preserve the original template.
segments.caption: RACM Templates

segments.text: Creating and Uploading RACMs lets you build new matrices from scratch or upload them via Excel. The create-new workflow guides you through defining the matrix header — entity, business process, risk category, and period — then adding controls row by row with fields for control description, frequency, owner, evidence requirements, and test procedures. For bulk uploads, the Excel import feature is powerful: you select your file, then the column mapping screen appears where you match each spreadsheet column to the corresponding RACM field — control number, description, risk rating, control type, owner, frequency, and so on. We'll walk through the mapping interface, showing how to handle required versus optional fields, set default values, and validate the mapping before proceeding. We'll stop at the final confirmation screen, not executing the import.
segments.caption: Creating & Uploading RACMs

segments.text: RACM Management is the central hub for all your Risk and Control Matrices. The main grid displays every RACM with columns for control number, description, entity, business process, risk rating, control type, frequency, current status, assigned owner, last tested date, and next due date. Powerful filters let you slice by entity, process, risk rating, status, or owner. Notice the two critical notifications at the top: one RACM pending change request — this indicates a process owner has requested a modification that needs coordinator review — and one RACM found ineffective — flagged during testing. We'll click into each notification to show the detail views. For the change request, you see the requested changes, rationale, and can approve, reject, or request more information. For the ineffective RACM, you see the test results, deficiency details, and can initiate a deficiency response workflow. We'll explore both up to the action buttons but not submit.
segments.caption: RACM Management

segments.text: RACM Assignment allows you to assign RACMs to process owners and approvers across the organization. The assignment matrix shows each RACM alongside its current owner, primary approver, backup approver, assignment status, and due date. You can bulk-assign by selecting multiple RACMs and choosing owners from the dropdown. The reminder configuration panel lets you set due date reminders — first reminder at three days, second at two days, final at one day — and escalation rules. There's also a reassignment workflow for when owners change roles. We'll demonstrate selecting a batch of RACMs, opening the assignment dialog, choosing new owners, setting due dates, and reviewing the reminder schedule — stopping before the final assign button.
segments.caption: RACM Assignment

segments.text: The Reports section provides comprehensive reporting on RACM status, compliance metrics, and audit trails. Available reports include: RACM Status Summary — showing counts by status across entities; Compliance Dashboard — tracking testing completion rates, overdue items, and trend lines; Change Request Log — every requested change with status and approver; Deficiency Tracker — all identified deficiencies with remediation status; Testing Evidence Report — detailed evidence collected per control; and Audit Trail — complete history of all actions. Each report can be filtered by date range, entity, process, or owner, and exported to PDF or Excel. We'll generate a sample RACM Status Summary for the current quarter, apply entity filters, and show the export options.
segments.caption: Reports

segments.text: RACM Change Requests manages the workflow for requesting and approving changes to existing RACMs. Navigating to the company coordinator RACM management page, we see the pending change request notification we noticed earlier. Clicking View opens the change request detail: the original control values, the proposed changes, the requester's justification, supporting documents, and the approval chain. The workflow shows current status — pending coordinator review — with buttons to Approve, Reject, or Request Clarification. If approved, the changes apply immediately; if rejected, the requester is notified with comments. We'll walk through each tab — Details, History, Documents — and hover over the action buttons to explain the consequences, but we won't click Approve or Reject to avoid modifying production data.
segments.caption: RACM Change Requests

segments.text: Deficiency Response Submission handles responses to identified control deficiencies. When a control is marked ineffective, the process owner receives a notification and must submit a remediation plan. The response form captures: root cause analysis, corrective action description, responsible person, target completion date, and required evidence. There's also a field for interim controls while the fix is implemented. Once submitted, the response routes to the coordinator for review — who can accept, request revision, or escalate. We'll open a sample deficiency response, fill in each field with example data, attach a sample evidence document, and show the submission confirmation dialog — stopping before the final Submit button.
segments.caption: Deficiency Response Submission

segments.text: Risk Analysis displays generated risks for specific units and processes. Selecting the APL1 unit and P2P Business Process filter shows the pre-generated risk register. Each risk entry includes: risk ID, description, inherent risk rating, key controls mapped, residual risk rating, risk owner, and last assessment date. You can drill into any risk to see the full bow-tie analysis — causes, consequences, preventive controls, detective controls. The Generate Risks button uses the AI engine to suggest new risks based on process descriptions, industry benchmarks, and historical data — we'll click it to show the generation dialog with parameter options. Similarly, Design Gap Analysis evaluates whether existing controls adequately address identified risks — it shows coverage gaps, missing control mappings, and suggestions for new controls. We'll open the Design Gap view for the same APL1 and P2P combination to demonstrate the side-by-side comparison.
segments.caption: Risk Analysis

segments.text: That concludes the IFC coordinator demo. You've seen the full workflow from user management through risk analysis, including all notification-driven processes like change requests and deficiency responses — all demonstrated up to the point of database modification, so no production data was changed. Thank you for watching.
segments.caption: Demo Complete
